name: Battle of Cannae

phases.title: The armies draw up facing each other
phases.text: The Romans faced east with the Aufidus on their right and massed their infantry deep in the centre. Hannibal put the Hispanic and Gallic infantry in the middle, the African infantry at the ends of the infantry line and the cavalry on the flanks.

phases.title: Hannibal advances his centre in a crescent
phases.text: As the armies advanced, Hannibal took the Hispanic and Gallic companies forward from the middle of his line. The flanking companies fell back behind them, so that the line curved out towards the Romans and the Africans were kept in reserve.

phases.title: The cavalry clash on both flanks
phases.text: The battle opened with a fierce cavalry fight on the flanks. On the Roman right the Hispanic and Gallic horse fought hard, and on the other flank the Numidians kept the Roman allied cavalry busy.

phases.title: The Roman right wing is driven back
phases.text: The Carthaginian horse got the upper hand and cut down the Roman cavalry on the right without giving quarter. The Roman right wing retreated, and Hasdrubal did not chase it.

phases.title: Hasdrubal rides across and the allied cavalry breaks
phases.text: Hasdrubal led his victorious horse to the other side of the field to attack the allied cavalry. Assailed from both sides, the allies broke before he reached them, and the Numidians pursued them off the field.

phases.title: The centre gives way step by step
phases.text: The Roman heavy infantry pressed forward and Hannibal held his men together in a controlled retreat. The curve buckled inwards as the Romans advanced and reserve lines pushed into the gaps.

phases.title: The Carthaginian cavalry attacks the Roman rear
phases.text: With the Roman cavalry driven off on both flanks, the Carthaginian horse had time to ride round and attack the Roman centre from behind.

phases.title: The Africans turn in against the Roman flanks
phases.text: Hannibal ordered the African infantry to turn inwards and advance against the Roman flanks. Together with the cavalry behind, this formed a pincer round the Roman infantry.

phases.title: The Romans are enclosed and killed
phases.text: Enclosed in a pocket with no means of escape, the Roman infantry was cut down by the cavalry behind it, the African infantry on both sides and the centre in front.

note: The Carthaginian left lay to the south by the Aufidus and the Romans faced east, so north is drawn at the top. The day falls on 2 August 216 BCE by the Roman calendar and on 1 July by one modern reckoning, so no date is shown. Varro held the Roman left and Paullus the right by the usual telling, though Samuels doubted who commanded where. Where the village of Cannae lay is not stated, so the village is not drawn. The paths of the cavalry are drawn straight; the accounts do not give their routes.
